claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced high-temperature plastic strain relative to pure tungsten.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced high-temperature toughness relative to pure tungsten.
The compositional complexity of WTaTiVZr induces large lattice distortions.
The compositional complexity of WTaTiVZr promotes in situ formation of coherent nano-precipitates.
Coherent nano-precipitates and lattice distortions inhibit localized dislocation pile-up.
Coherent nano-precipitates and lattice distortions promote distributed plasticity.
Coherent nano-precipitates and lattice distortions reduce crack-tip stress concentrations during high-temperature loading.
The microstructural obstacles in WTaTiVZr enable more uniform plastic flow and dynamic recovery.
Pure tungsten lacks the hypothesized coherent nano-precipitates and associated multicomponent lattice distortions.
Pure tungsten exhibits more localized deformation and brittleness than WTaTiVZr under comparable high-temperature conditions.
Elevated-temperature creep behavior of TaTiVWZr has previously been studied and compared with pure tungsten.
Coherent precipitation can produce substantial strengthening effects in refractory high-entropy alloys, while suitable precipitation architectures are pursued to retain ductility.
At approximately 800 °C, WTaTiVZr is predicted to show greater tensile plastic strain than matched pure tungsten.
At approximately 800 °C, WTaTiVZr is predicted to show higher fracture toughness than matched pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr is predicted to have a more uniform dislocation distribution than pure tungsten after high-temperature loading.
Pure tungsten is predicted to undergo more localized crack propagation than WTaTiVZr.
Matching grain size, heat treatment, and loading conditions is intended to isolate composition-dependent microstructural effects.
Irradiation, thermal-history differences, or substantial grain-structure differences may mask or alter the proposed response.
Grain-boundary sliding may also contribute to the high-temperature deformation behavior.
Failure to observe statistically significant improvements in both plastic strain and fracture toughness, or failure to observe the proposed microstructural mediators, would refute the hypothesis.
